A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TraceGrad research. All 22 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v3, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures that can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: Tables 1–2 report original TraceGrad and component-ablation results on six crystal benchmarks. Appendix A additionally reports HarmoSE+TraceGrad experiments.

after.justification: Tables 1–4 report TraceGrad experiments using DeepH-E3 and QHNet across eight benchmarks, including downstream physical quantities. Appendix F retains the component-ablation results.

M1.justification: The trace supervision, gradient-induced equivariant features, weighted Clebsch–Gordan construction, residual connections, decoders, adaptive two-term MSE loss and inference procedure remain unchanged. QHNet instantiates the existing general backbone interface; no TraceGrad-specific procedural adaptation is described. The newly stated hidden width is implementation disclosure.

E1.justification: v3 retains the six crystal datasets and adds QH9-Stable and QH9-Dynamic molecular systems containing C, H, O, N and F. Coverage expands to molecular size and trajectory extrapolation, together with evaluation of downstream occupied-orbital energies and electronic wavefunctions.

E2.justification: v3 adds QHNet as the evaluated comparator on QH9 and removes v1 Appendix A's MoS2 comparison involving HarmoSE and DeepH-2. DeepHE3, renamed DeepH-E3, and its component-ablation variants remain. Thus an entire comparison branch is removed while a different backbone comparison is introduced.

E3.justification: The new QH9 evaluations use atom-count-disjoint 'ood' and trajectory-disjoint 'mol' splits, diagonal/interatomic Hamiltonian-block MAEs, orbital-energy MAE and wavefunction cosine similarity. They introduce a batch-16 AdamW configuration and conversion of cited baseline MAEs to meV. Existing DeepH splits and metrics remain unchanged; newly disclosed crystal training settings do not establish protocol revisions.

E4.justification: v3 adds distribution-shift evaluations of molecular atom-count extrapolation and unseen thermal-motion trajectories. It removes the approximately equivariant HarmoSE compatibility case study from v1 Appendix A. The original Trace-only/Grad-only ablations, twisted-crystal tests and block-error analyses are retained, with the ablations and complete block plots moved to Appendices E–F.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten repeated experiments, mean-only result tables and a standard-deviation bound around 0.007 meV for Hamiltonian errors. v3 omits v1's explicit seed value of 42 while retaining the fixed-seed statement. No increase in repeated runs or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: The crystal and component-ablation values are unchanged. v3 Tables 3–4 add QHNet versus QHNet+TraceGrad Hamiltonian MAEs of 1.962 versus 1.191 meV on QS and 4.733 versus 2.819 meV on QD. QD orbital-energy MAE is 264.483 versus 63.375 meV, and cosine similarity increases from 0.792 to 0.927, contrary to Section 4's 'lowers' wording. The earlier HarmoSE comparison results are removed.

T1.justification: The two equivariance theorems, their proofs and the weighted Clebsch–Gordan construction are mathematically retained despite relocation and equivalent notation. Section 6.3 adds a brief complexity argument that featurewise TraceGrad processing preserves the backbones' O(N) scaling; v1 discussed linear scaling only for deep-learning approaches generally.

C1.justification: The foundational claim of reconciling equivariance and nonlinear expressiveness remains. v3 expands the central empirical contribution beyond Hamiltonian accuracy on six crystal benchmarks to demonstrated molecular extrapolation and downstream physical-quantity accuracy, explicitly claiming up to 76% improvement in orbital-energy prediction and 17% in wavefunction similarity.

C2.justification: v3 adds specific interpretations of size/trajectory extrapolation, robustness to thermal motion, SOC modeling and downstream physical utility. The trace/gradient complementarity explanation remains essentially unchanged. The earlier argument that success with HarmoSE demonstrates compatibility with approximately equivariant architectures is removed.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies a hidden width of 1024, per-dataset learning rates, Adam with batch size 1 for the crystal datasets, and AdamW with batch size 16 for QH9. Appendix C adds atom-count ranges and molecular split statistics. This substantially expands implementation documentation beyond v1's activation, normalization and loss-weight details, without establishing changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds QHNet, QH9, KAN, Transformer-survey and twisted-material references. It removes the detailed hybrid-method discussion of Yin et al. and expands the EquiformerV2 critique to tensor-order pruning. Yin et al.'s retitled reference is the same retained work; the overall equivariance–expressiveness positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: the related-method analysis and theorem proofs move to Appendices A–B, the lengthy application section is condensed into the introduction/results, and ablation descriptions move to Appendix F. The abstract, results discussion and future-work section are extensively revised.

P2.justification: v3 separates main comparisons from full ablation tables, adds QH9 and dataset-statistics tables, splits the structural illustrations, and recolors and rearranges the block-error plots. A selected-panel summary appears in the main text while complete plots move to the appendix. The HarmoSE table and plot are removed; retained plot data remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the framework's generality and physical usefulness. Tables 3–4 test another strictly equivariant backbone on molecular size/trajectory extrapolation and evaluate downstream quantities absent from v1's matrix-error-only experiments. Added training details also improve reproducibility. Removing the HarmoSE/DeepH-2 study narrows comparative evidence, and the missing seed value and incorrect similarity-direction wording are regressions, but the new validation resolves important gaps in the earlier paper's support for broad applicability.
